title: Help me to believe or help me to unbelieve?
html_source:
Stephen twists the language of Mark 9:24, which, in context is pretty hard to read any way other than an anguished father begging Jesus for help in believing more deeply so that his son will be healed.

But in a vacuum, the phrase could be read the other way: Please help strengthen my unbelief.

If the unbelief is unbelief in God, then it would be odd to ask God to help you form a stronger unbelief, so Stephen carries that question into the next few sentences.
